body:
Certares has closed a single-asset continuation fund for Guardian Alarm, providing existing investors with a liquidity option while committing additional capital to support the security and fire services company’s acquisition strategy and continued expansion.

The new investor group was led by funds managed by New 2ND Capital, a New York-based private equity firm specializing in GP-led secondary transactions. Financial terms of the transaction and the amount of additional capital committed to Guardian were not disclosed.

The transaction allows Certares to extend its ownership partnership with Guardian while giving existing shareholders the choice to realize liquidity. At the same time, the continuation vehicle provides fresh capital that Guardian can deploy into acquisitions and investments supporting organic growth.

Founded in 1930 and headquartered in Southfield, Michigan, Guardian provides security, fire, access control and automation systems to commercial and residential customers across more than 10 states in the Midwest and South.

The company operates a vertically integrated model spanning system design and installation, 24/7 in-house monitoring, service, maintenance and inspections. That structure gives Guardian control over much of the customer relationship while supporting recurring revenue from monitoring and other ongoing services.

“The additional capital provided through this transaction will allow us to continue investing in the business and accelerate our acquisition strategy as we expand Guardian’s presence in existing and new markets,” Guardian CEO Brent Uhl said.

For Guardian, the continuation fund creates additional financial capacity to pursue consolidation opportunities without requiring Certares to exit its investment. The structure also brings New 2ND into the investor group as Guardian seeks to build additional geographic density and expand into new markets.

Certares Managing Director Richard Moreau said the investment firm plans to continue supporting Guardian through its next phase of organic and acquisition-driven growth.

The continuation vehicle reflects a strategy increasingly used in private equity to retain ownership of portfolio companies beyond the traditional holding period while offering liquidity to investors in an existing fund. In Guardian’s case, the structure allows Certares to maintain exposure to the company’s future growth while introducing new capital specifically positioned to support the next stage of the business.

New 2ND focuses on these types of GP-led secondary transactions in North American middle-market companies. The firm said Guardian’s established market position, recurring revenue model and growth history were important factors behind its investment.

“Guardian represents exactly the type of high-quality business we seek to support through our secondary investments,” New 2ND partner Rob Luttrell said. “The Company has an established market position, a compelling recurring revenue model, and a demonstrated track record of growth.”

Guardian’s acquisition strategy provides one of the primary avenues for deploying the new capital. The company can use acquisitions to expand its presence in existing regions, enter additional markets and add customer accounts to a centralized operating and monitoring infrastructure.

That model can create operating leverage as acquired businesses and customer relationships are incorporated into Guardian’s broader platform. Its combination of installation, monitoring and ongoing service also provides multiple points of engagement throughout the lifecycle of a security or fire system.

Certares Managing Director Zach Lazar said Guardian has developed a scalable operating platform under Uhl and his management team, providing a foundation for continued expansion.

The transaction also represents an extension of Certares’ investment strategy beyond its travel and hospitality focus. The alternative asset manager also invests in business and consumer services companies and had approximately $6.4 billion in regulatory assets under management as of Dec. 31, 2025.

New 2ND had approximately $2.6 billion in regulatory assets under management at the end of 2025 and is currently investing its fourth fund.

With the continuation fund completed, Guardian gains additional acquisition capital while maintaining its existing relationship with Certares and adding New 2ND as an investment partner. The structure positions the company to continue consolidating security and fire services businesses while investing in its vertically integrated platform and expanding its footprint across existing and new U.S. markets.

William Blair served as exclusive financial advisor to Certares and Guardian. White & Case and Sidley Austin served as legal advisors to Certares and Guardian, while Ropes & Gray advised New 2ND.
